target_customer: Small field-service and construction teams, and SMBs more broadly, that coordinate work through paper, text messages and legacy desktop software
problem: Field teams track time, materials, photos and notes on paper or by text message, which managers cannot see in real time. The YC directory describes the product as calendar and messaging for SMBs.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (a third-party directory lists pricing from $29 per month, unverified)
product_category: Mobile work tracking, calendar and messaging for small business field teams

founders.name: Zane Salim
founders.background_notes: The YC company page lists Zane Salim as Founder/CEO with a one-line bio and no education or employers. The YC launch post names no founders. A search snippet attributed two further co-founders to a YC Stripe Medium post, but that page returned 403 and was not opened, so they are not listed.

competitors.name: Paper based tracking
competitors.what: Paper forms and logs, the incumbent for field teams
competitors.traction_then: The YC launch post says about 61% of field teams still used paper

competitors.name: Sage (legacy desktop software)
competitors.what: Legacy desktop business software named by the launch post as an alternative

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app plus web dashboard with templates for time, materials and photos is standard engineering for a small team in 2017.

defensibility.rationale: Field work tracking apps were easy to copy, and the launch post cites text messages and paper as the main rivals, which signals low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Fibo. The company is listed inactive without a public cause.

market_need_then: The YC launch post cites about 61% of field teams still using paper, and construction and landscaping crews lacked real time visibility for managers.

branding.domain_note: Used fiboapp.com, an app suffix domain, not the exact .com.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found. Several unrelated companies share the Fibo name, including an Israeli tax refund service and a crypto wallet.

outcome_analysis: Fibo joined YC in Winter 2017 with a field team work tracking product and a 15 person team, but the YC directory later described it as calendar and messaging for SMBs and marks it inactive. No shutdown announcement or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned. Databases disagree sharply on funding, from about $120K to a reported $2M seed, which prevents any judgment on whether capital was the constraint.
notes: fiboapp.com returned HTTP 503 so the site is treated as dead or unreachable. The launch post describes work tracking for field teams while the YC directory describes calendar and messaging for SMBs, so the positioning may have shifted. Funding rests on databases only: CB Insights reports about $120K over 3 rounds with Tango.vc, Bossa Invest and Y Combinator as investors, with seed rounds dated 2017-03-21 and 2017-04-10 and a 2022-03-04 round that looks like a data artifact for an inactive company. StartupIntros alone reports a $2M seed in April 2017, which conflicts with the $120K total and may duplicate the CB April round. Amounts for the CB rounds are not shown. Rounds seen only in one database.
